StarTech's DisplayLink support FAQ says macOS 10.15 or later requires DisplayLink Manager plus the required Screen Recording/accessibility permissions; if the app is not running or permissions are disabled, DisplayLink-driven external displays may not appear. Source

On StarTech's official IT Pro Community, a MacBook Pro M3 user reported the second DisplayLink monitor going black when Screen Recording permission was disabled; StarTech support explained that the permission is required for the virtual display path. This is a DisplayLink support case, not a 129N-specific reliability test. Source

Rear HDMI and MFDP USB-C video paths are muxed and cannot both be used as simultaneous video outputs; non-Thunderbolt hosts lose Thunderbolt features.

Dell troubleshooting says monitor count and resolution depend on the host graphics path; with Intel graphics plus the system LCD, only two displays may be supported, while discrete Nvidia/AMD configurations can support three external displays plus the system LCD. Dell also recommends a dock power-cycle sequence for flicker or USB failures. Source

A Dell Community WD22TB4 case reports dual-4K HBR2 behavior falling from 60Hz to 30Hz after reconnecting the dock, with connection-order workarounds discussed in the official community thread. Treat this as a user/support case, not a universal WD22TB4 fact. Source

Original M1 Macs do not support dual external displays through TS4; USB-C hosts have reduced functionality and 2.5Gb Ethernet is Thunderbolt-host dependent.

CalDigit's TS4 support knowledge base documents shared bandwidth groups: many USB ports share the same 10Gbps USB hub, while DisplayPort and downstream Thunderbolt ports share the same 40Gbps Thunderbolt bandwidth. High-bandwidth peripherals therefore compete within those groups rather than receiving dedicated bandwidth. Source
